quote: Alle ganzen ganzzahlige Funktion von $x$ finden, welche [-...-] gleich $\frac{F}{p^n}$ [-..-] sind, wo $F$ eine ganze ganzzahlige Funktion von den gegebenen ganzen ganzzahlige Funktion $\varphi, \psi, \chi, \ldots$ von $x$ [-sind-] ist und $p$ eine gegebene oder auch eine willkürliche Primzahl und $n$ eine [-..-] beliebige ganze Zahl ist!
english: Find all integral integer-coefficient functions of x which are equal to F/p^n, where F is an integral integer-coefficient function of the given integral integer-coefficient functions φ, ψ, χ, ... of x, and p is a given or also an arbitrary prime and n is an arbitrary integer!
topic: Notes on continuous deformation of forms within a class (binary moduli), a determinant-quotient representation of the resultant obtained from Hilbert's truncation (Abbrech) procedure and its link to Noether's theorem, and the problem of finding all integral integer-valued functions of the form F/p^n.

triage.modern_statement: Take finitely many polynomials φ, ψ, χ, … in Z[x] and let A = Z[φ, ψ, χ, …] be the subring of Z[x] they generate. The question is to describe every polynomial G in Z[x] such that p^n·G lies in A for some n ≥ 0. Here p is either one fixed prime or any prime. For a fixed p this is the ring Z[x] ∩ A[1/p], the p-saturation of A in Z[x]. If p may be any prime, the ring becomes Z[x] ∩ Q[φ, ψ, χ, …]. Hilbert probably wanted a finite generating system or a way to construct all such G. This is a version of the finite-generation question for rings of the form L ∩ (polynomial ring), but over the integers rather than over a field, and in one variable x.
triage.answered_by: I found no source that answers this exact integer-coefficient question. The closest well-known problem is Hilbert's 14th problem (1900). It asks whether L ∩ k[x_1,…,x_n] is finitely generated when k is a field and L is a subfield of k(x_1,…,x_n). Zariski (1954) proved this whenever tr.deg_k L ≤ 2, which settles it for n ≤ 2. Nagata gave the first counterexamples, and Daigle–Freudenburg (n = 5) and Freudenburg (n = 6) gave later ones. All of this concerns coefficients in a field, not the Z[x] version with denominators p^n in this note.

evidence.claim: Hilbert's 14th problem asks whether L ∩ k[X] is finitely generated, where L is a subfield of k(X) containing k.
Zariski showed the answer is yes when tr.deg L ≤ 2, so the problem holds for n ≤ 2. Freudenburg (n = 6) and Daigle–Freudenburg (n = 5) gave counterexamples.
Zariski's finiteness theorem: if A is a normal finitely generated domain over a field k and L has tr.deg_k L ≤ 2, then L ∩ A is finitely generated.
Hilbert's 14th problem, posed in 1900, asks whether certain algebras are finitely generated. Nagata constructed the first counterexamples.

triage.why: The note is a well-posed research question: find the saturation of a subring generated by given polynomials in Z[x] with respect to a prime p, or with respect to all primes. Its form, 'all integral functions that become expressible after allowing a denominator', is the same as the L ∩ polynomial-ring setup of Hilbert's 14th problem, and that problem has a known history (Zariski, Nagata, Freudenburg, Daigle). However, the 14th problem as published and studied works over a field, and the published sources I found do not cover this one-variable version over Z with denominators p^n. So I cannot tie it to a specific solution or call it the same as the 14th problem. My searches were limited, so a specific treatment may exist that I did not find. Algorithmic subalgebra-membership methods might apply, but I found no source confirming that, so I do not claim it.
